Given \(f(x)+f'(x)+f''(x)=x^5+64\).

Differentiating,

\(f'(x)+f''(x)+f'''(x)=5x^4\)

Again differentiating,

\(f''(x)+f'''(x)+f^{iv}(x)=20x^3\)

Again differentiating,

Subtracting,

\(f(1)+f'(1)+f''(1)=65\)

\(\Rightarrow 0+f'(1)+80=65\)

\(\Rightarrow f'(1)=-15\)

Therefore,

\(\displaystyle \lim_{x\to1}\dfrac{f(x)}{x-1}=-15\)

Consider the following two propositions:

\(P_1: \sim(p \rightarrow \sim q) \)

\(P_2:(p \wedge \sim q) \wedge((\sim p) \vee q)\)

If the proposition \( p \rightarrow((\sim p) \vee q) \) is evaluated as FALSE, then:

 

[JEE Main 2022, 25 June (Shift 1)]
options: \( P_{1} \) is TRUE and \( P_{2} \) is FALSE
\( P_{1} \) is FALSE and \( P_{2} \) is TRUE
questions.explanation:
The implication \(p\Rightarrow((\sim p)\vee q)\) is false.

An implication is false only when its antecedent is true and its consequent is false.

\(\Rightarrow p=T\)

\(\Rightarrow (\sim p)\vee q=F\)

\(\Rightarrow \sim p=F\) and \(q=F\)

For \(P_1=\sim(p\Rightarrow\sim q)\), we have \(\sim q=T\).

\(\Rightarrow P_1=\sim(T\Rightarrow T)=\sim T=F\)

For \(P_2=(p\wedge\sim q)\wedge((\sim p)\vee q)\), we get

\(\Rightarrow P_2=(T\wedge T)\wedge(F\vee F)=T\wedge F=F\)

Both \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) are false.

The correct option is \(\mathrm{C}\).

Let \( C_{r} \) denote the binomial coefficient of \( x^{r} \) in the expansion of \( (1+x)^{10} \). If \( \alpha, \beta \in R, C_{1}+3 \cdot 2 C_{2}+5 \cdot 3 C_{3}+\ldots \) upto 10 terms \( =\frac{\alpha \times 2^{11}}{2^{\beta}-1}\left(C_{0}+\frac{C_{1}}{2}+\frac{C_{2}}{3}+\ldots\right. \) upto 10 terms \( ) \), then the value of \( \alpha+\beta \) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2022, 25 June (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(F(x)=(1+x)^{10}=\displaystyle\sum_{r=0}^{10}C_rx^r\).

The left-hand side is \(S=\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{10}r(2r-1)C_r\).

Since \(r(2r-1)=2r(r-1)+r\),

we get \(S=2\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{10}r(r-1)C_r+\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{10}rC_r\).

Using derivatives of \(F(x)\) at \(x=1\),

\(\displaystyle\sum r(r-1)C_r=10\cdot 9\cdot 2^8\) and \(\displaystyle\sum rC_r=10\cdot 2^9\)

Therefore, \(S=2(10\cdot 9\cdot 2^8)+10\cdot 2^9=100\cdot 2^9\)

Also, \(T=\displaystyle\sum_{r=0}^{10}\dfrac{C_r}{r+1}\)

Integrating \(F(x)\) from \(0\) to \(1\),

we get \(T=\displaystyle\int_0^1(1+x)^{10}\,dx=\dfrac{2^{11}-1}{11}\).

Thus the intended equation becomes \(100\cdot 2^9=\dfrac{\alpha\cdot 2^{11}}{2^\beta-1}\cdot\dfrac{2^{11}-1}{11}\).

The standard intended comparison takes \(\beta=11\).

Then \(100\cdot 2^9=\dfrac{\alpha\cdot 2^{11}}{11}\),

so \(\alpha=275\)

Hence the intended value is \(\alpha+\beta=275+11=286\).
